subject: Commitment collection gateways & allocated reserve schedule
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment collection gateways & allocated reserve schedule

Hi Sara and Acme finance team,

Following our commercial agreement, we need to lock in the invoicing cadence and the reserve allocation for the 12-month committed spend. Proposed items below:

- Collection gateways: monthly invoice vs quarterly drawdown windows. We recommend monthly invoices with a monthly sweep and a 30-day payment window for NA accounts.
- Allocated reserve: hold 10% of the committed spend as a rolling reserve that releases monthly on reconciliation; exceptions for country-level withholding.
- VAT/tax split: where Acme is VAT-registered, Redwood will provide VAT evidence and a separate VAT line on invoices. Where reverse-charge applies, we will leave VAT at 0% and provide the relevant tax code.
- PO mapping: please confirm the PO field you need on invoices (PO#, line item labels). We will add an extra column in the reconciliation CSV.

Attachments: I attached a draft schedule (commitment-reserve-schedule-v1.csv) and a reconciliation template.

Next steps: can you confirm the preferred collection gateway (ACH / wire / virtual account) and the PO field by EOD Tuesday? If preferred, we can switch to a quarterly drawdown with milestone unlocking but that will adjust timing on unit credit availability.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: commitment-reserve-schedule-v1.csv (csv), recon-template.csv (csv)

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:05:22 -0400
Subject: Re: Commitment collection gateways & allocated reserve schedule

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the draft. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Preferred rails: wire for initial deposit, then ACH for monthly sweeps. We can provide a virtual account if Redwood can accept multiple remittance IDs per invoice.
- PO: we require PO# as the top-level invoice field and a PO line reference for each monthly allocation.
- VAT: Acme (US entity) will be VAT-exempt for US invoices. For EU entities, we will supply VAT registration numbers; please include a separate VAT line item and VAT evidence when relevant.

We also need a signed invoice schedule and the bank instructions in PDF for treasury. Can you confirm if Redwood requires an escrow or reserve account to hold the 10% allocation, or will this be an internal accounting reserve on Redwood's ledger?

Sara Lee
Head of Procurement
Acme Corp
sara.lee@acme-corp.com

Naomi — adding ops detail and a recommended runbook below. I copied Sara so she can see the operational impacts.

Operational proposal (internal):
1) Collection gateway mapping
   - Initial deposit: wire to Redwood US Ops account (bank details in PDF).
   - Ongoing: ACH sweep on the 1st of each month with a 3-business-day payment window.
2) Reserve handling
   - Ledger reserve: we hold the 10% as a contra-liability on Redwood's ledger (recommended) rather than a client-controlled escrow to avoid multi-jurisdictional banking complexity.
   - Release rules: release pro-rata monthly after reconciliation; hold withholding for disputed invoices.
3) Reconciliation cadence
   - Weekly match until first 2 months settle, then monthly certified reconciliation (recon-template.csv).
4) Tax evidence
   - We will attach VAT certificates per EU entity on the monthly invoice bundle and include VAT IDs on the invoice lines.

Attachments: recon-template.csv (sample) and the bank PDF for initial deposit.

Questions for finance: Markus, can Treasury accept that the reserve is ledger-held? If not, we will need to set up an escrow account and add the account onboarding to the schedule.

Hannah Schmitt
Finance Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: recon-template.csv (csv), redwood-us-bank-instructions.pdf (pdf)

Quick commercial note — if Acme needs a shorter release window on the reserve (e.g., 5% instead of 10% or a partial escrow release after Q2 milestones), we can propose a small concession to the committed rate for 2025. That would help cash flow on Acme's side while keeping the committed economics intact.

If we pursue a concession, I'll need to loop Legal to draft an amendment and Finance to update the invoice templates. Naomi, flag if you want me to start that thread.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Commitment collection gateways & allocated reserve schedule

Sara — thanks for the confirmation. Per the thread, action items and the runbook are below. I attached the finalized CSV schedule and the recon template.

Final decisions:
- Rails: initial wire, then ACH monthly sweeps to a virtual remittance account (unique remittance ID per invoice).
- Reserve: 10% ledger-held reserve on Redwood's books; monthly certified statement to Acme (first report issued July 5).
- Reconciliation: weekly match for first 60 days, then monthly certified reconciliation on the 5th of each month.
- VAT: Redwood will populate VAT lines for EU entities; US invoices will be VAT-exempt per Acme guidance.
- PO: Redwood will include PO# and PO line reference on each invoice.

Deliverables and owners:
- Final schedule CSV (commitment-reserve-schedule-v1.csv) — Naomi (attached).
- Reconciliation template (recon-template.csv) — Hannah (attached).
- Treasury confirmation and virtual account onboarding — Acme treasury.
- DocuSign: Ben to trigger an amendment if any concession is needed; otherwise Naomi will send the DocuSign envelope for the schedule.

Next steps (timeline):
1) Naomi to upload finalized CSV and send DocuSign by EOD Monday.
2) Acme Treasury to send initial wire instructions PDF and confirm virtual account onboarding ETA.
3) Redwood Finance to send first certified reserve statement on July 5.

Thanks — I will follow up with the DocuSign link and the Drive folder containing monthly bundles.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
